recommendations.claim: Daily energy target of 2150 kcal supports recovery without imposing a deficit on a modestly-eating returning trainee at ~75 kg body mass; protein set at 128 g (~1.7 g/kg) to meet the evidence-supported training-recovery floor, carbohydrates at 240 g to restore muscle glycogen, fat at 60 g meeting essential fatty acid needs.
recommendations.source: Morton et al. 2018 (Br J Sports Med) meta-analysis on protein dose; Thomas et al. 2016 ACSM/AND/DC joint position stand
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: moderate / strength: strong / causal (daily protein total for recovery)
recommendations.reversibility: Calorie target is upward-adjustable as appetite returns; protein floor is the binding constraint.

recommendations.claim: Breakfast of eggs, oats, and fruit supplies leucine-sufficient protein (~35 g) plus carbohydrate to break the overnight fast and prime tissue repair.
recommendations.source: Norton & Layman 2006 (J Nutr) on leucine threshold; ACSM/AND/DC 2016 position stand
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: low / strength: conditional / causal (distribution is lower-certainty than the daily total)

meal.name: Breakfast
meal.contents: 3 whole eggs scrambled, 80 g rolled oats cooked, 150 g mixed berries, 200 ml low-fat milk

recommendations.claim: Lunch of chicken, rice, and vegetables delivers a second leucine-triggering protein bolus (~40 g) with glycogen-replenishing carbohydrate.
recommendations.source: Areta et al. 2013 (J Physiol) on protein distribution; Thomas et al. 2016 position stand
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: low / strength: conditional / causal (distribution is lower-certainty than the daily total)
recommendations.reversibility: Protein source interchangeable; carbohydrate portion adjustable.

meal.name: Lunch
meal.contents: 170 g grilled chicken breast, 180 g cooked rice, 200 g mixed vegetables with olive oil

recommendations.claim: Dinner of salmon, potato, and leafy greens closes the daily protein target (~33 g) while supplying omega-3 fatty acids with provisional anti-inflammatory signaling evidence.
recommendations.source: Smith et al. 2011 (Clin Sci) on omega-3 and MPS; Calder 2017 (Eur J Clin Nutr) on EPA/DHA and inflammation
recommendations.confidence_tier: certainty: low / strength: conditional / associational (omega-3 anti-inflammatory benefit is associational)
recommendations.reversibility: Fish source substitutable; fat-soluble vitamin delivery from this meal is food-first per protocol.

meal.name: Dinner
meal.contents: 150 g baked salmon fillet, 200 g boiled baby potatoes, 150 g sauteed spinach and courgette

energy_budget.bounce_reason: A ~700 kcal session against a constrained ~2,050 kcal intake at maintenance drives the day to roughly a 650 kcal deficit, which programs an unintended deficit into a recovery-priority trainee whose appetite has not expanded to cover the load.
